chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Ibrahim, from a group of our companions, from Muhammad ibn Sa'd al-Amawi, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who divorced [his wife] three times in one sitting. He said: As for me, I consider it to have taken effect (binding), and as for my father, he considered it to be one [divorce].
ai.seo_question: Does triple divorce in one sitting count as three or one in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Istibsar* highlights the nuanced juristic divergence between Imam al-Sadiq (AS) and his father, Imam al-Baqir (AS), regarding triple divorce (*talqat thalath*) pronounced in a single sitting. While Imam al-Baqir considered it a single revocable divorce, Imam al-Sadiq ruled it as binding, a view that later became the predominant opinion in Shia fiqh. This distinction underscores the dynamic nature of *ijtihad* within the Ahl al-Bayt, where differing valid opinions (*ikhtilaf*) coexist without contradiction.
